skill.name: lead-generation-popup-specialist
skill.description: Plan, write, audit, and improve website lead-capture popups and forms, including offers, coupons, targeting, timing, experiments, and subscriber email follow-up. Use for onsite conversion campaigns, not cold outreach or general advertising.
skill.summary: Design permission-based lead capture campaigns with actionable copy, targeting rules, email follow-up, and measurement plans.
skill.author: email-marketing-skills-hub

finding_verdicts.reason: The passage recommends concrete service inquiries and approved response times. It contains no system inspection instructions or reconnaissance commands.
The passage covers form validation and testing submission failures. These are application quality checks, not instructions to enumerate systems or collect host information.
The passage specifies viewport, keyboard, and screen-reader accessibility checks. It does not request host inspection or sensitive system information.
The passage links a public consent guide and discusses authorized sender authentication checks. No configuration library, environment variable access, or credential retrieval appears.
The passage explains benchmark eligibility, weighting, and sampling limitations. It describes aggregate marketing statistics, not system reconnaissance.
The URL cites the public Agent Skills specification without transmitting data or executing a request. The passage explicitly states drafting requires no network access.
The passage links a local measurement reference and defines campaign reporting metrics. It contains no host enumeration or system information collection.

content.value_statement: Poorly timed popups can interrupt visitors and collect contacts without improving business outcomes. This skill develops consent-aware campaigns with clear copy, targeting, follow-up, and measurement.
actual_capabilities: Draft popup headlines, supporting text, field labels, calls to action, error messages, and success states.
Specify visitor eligibility, display triggers, exclusions, dismissal behavior, frequency proposals, and post-conversion suppression.
Plan approved coupon offers with redemption terms and business outcome metrics.
Design resource delivery and subscriber follow-up with consent, unsubscribe, and suppression checks.
Define experiment hypotheses, measurement units, guardrails, and statistical assumptions.
Audit mobile usability, accessibility, integration failures, and launch readiness.
limitations: Campaign drafts do not authorize publication, contact exports, code installation, or email sending.
Live implementation requires an authorized execution environment or connector; otherwise, the skill provides setup instructions.
Vendor features, integrations, plan restrictions, and changing claims require current verification.
Recommendations do not guarantee conversion gains, inbox placement, or legal compliance.

use_cases.title: Plan a Welcome Offer
use_cases.description: Develop an approved coupon campaign with targeting, offer terms, fulfillment copy, and contribution margin guardrails.

use_cases.title: Capture Relevant Resource Requests
use_cases.description: Create a resource capture form with minimal fields, clear delivery expectations, consent handling, and qualified lead measurement.

use_cases.title: Audit Newsletter Signup Friction
use_cases.description: Review an inline form or popup for accessibility, interruption, repeat exposure, and honest success messaging.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Signup Copy
prompt_templates.prompt: Write newsletter signup copy for [audience] on [page]. Use [topic] and [cadence]. Include field labels, CTA, dismissal, error, and success text.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: create copy from a short brief.

prompt_templates.title: Specify a Capture Campaign
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a [resource or approved offer] campaign for [site] using [platform]. Define eligibility, triggers, exclusions, frequency, mobile behavior, and fulfillment. Label missing assumptions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: turn a brief into a campaign specification.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Capture and Follow-Up
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [public URL or supplied materials] for form friction, accessibility, consent, suppression, and email fulfillment. Prioritize evidence-based issues by impact, confidence, and effort.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: review an existing campaign without making live changes.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Controlled Experiment
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an experiment using [baseline], [eligible traffic], and [smallest worthwhile effect]. Define randomization, power assumptions, duration, qualified-lead outcomes, guardrails, and a decision rule.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: evaluate campaign changes with explicit measurement assumptions.

output_examples.input: Draft an inline signup for a weekly gardening newsletter, with no discount.
output: Headline: Get the Weekly Garden Checklist
Supporting text: Receive seasonal tasks and practical growing tips each week.
Error: Enter a valid email address.
Success: Your signup was received. Your first checklist will arrive by email.
Launch check: Verify the promised delivery before enabling this success message.

output_examples.input: We recorded 40 submissions across 2,000 popup views. Can we call these sales or unique leads?
output: Submission rate: 2.0%, based on 40 submissions and 2,000 recorded popup views.
This measures submissions per recorded view, not unique people, qualified leads, or sales.
Check duplicate submissions, consent status, integration receipts, and downstream outcomes before reporting lead quality.

output_examples.input: Review a popup that reopens after dismissal and reports success before email delivery is verified.
output: Priority 1: Separate receipt confirmation from delivery confirmation so the success state reflects the verified outcome.
Priority 2: Define dismissal suppression and test transitions across subsequent pages.
Launch checks: Verify duplicate submissions, integration timeouts, mobile close controls, and downstream delivery with approved test recipients.

best_practices: Provide the audience, page, goal, approved offer constraints, current platform, baseline, and available traffic.
Use aggregate metrics and synthetic examples; exclude customer records, credentials, and private account identifiers from reusable outputs.
Validate accessibility, consent transitions, suppression, and fulfillment before an explicitly authorized launch.
anti_patterns: Treating popup clicks or submissions as proof of consent, qualified leads, or revenue.
Using fabricated scarcity, preselected marketing consent, shaming dismissals, or unapproved coupon terms.
Declaring a test winner from an early favorable result or treating vendor benchmarks as guaranteed improvements.

faq.question: Does this skill require Poptin?
faq.answer: No. It supports the existing tool when suitable and can provide a platform-neutral setup plan.

faq.question: Can it publish campaigns automatically?
faq.answer: Drafting does not authorize publication. Live actions require explicit authorization and an available execution environment.

faq.question: Does it need network access?
faq.answer: Drafting does not require network access. Public page reviews and current product verification may require it.

faq.question: Can it guarantee higher conversion rates?
faq.answer: No. Recommendations are hypotheses, and benchmark comparisons are descriptive rather than proof of improvement.

faq.question: Can it plan subscriber emails?
faq.answer: Yes. It drafts fulfillment and follow-up plans with consent eligibility, unsubscribe handling, suppression, and delivery verification.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Share your audience, page, goal, approved offer, platform, traffic, and baseline. Missing details can become clearly labeled draft assumptions.
